accounting.rationale: J3/24-007 PDF 15, printed 1, lines 5-7: establishes document scope and purpose. It is not a processor obligation or an executable Fortran feature.
The document specifies the form and establishes the interpretation of programs in the base Fortran language; this scope sentence is not a separate owner for the actual forms or interpretations.
The purpose statement explains why the document exists; it does not require a measurable portability, reliability, maintainability, or efficiency result from any one processor.
PDF 15 lines 8-12 enumerate subject matter specified by the document. These are scope statements, not independently testable requirements.
The forms a Fortran program can take are within document scope, but this scope bullet does not create a separate grammar facet.
Rules for interpreting a program and its data are within document scope; this bullet is not a separate semantic owner.
Input data forms are within document scope; this bullet does not itself specify a concrete input/output requirement.
Output data forms are within document scope; this bullet does not itself specify a concrete input/output requirement.

PDF 15 lines 13-14 sets the default addressee for requirements and prohibitions: unless otherwise stated, they apply to programs rather than processors. Existing processor obligations named by the exception are registered in doc/catalogues/processor_conformance.json section 4.2.
PDF 15 lines 15-31 lists matters not specified by this document. The exclusions prevent inventing processor obligations or portable oracles from omitted implementation details.
The mechanism by which programs are transformed for computing systems is out of scope; this does not constrain compiler phases or object formats.
Setup and control operations for using programs on computing systems are out of scope.
Transcription of programs and data to or from storage media is out of scope.

Program and processor behavior where the document fails to establish an interpretation is out of scope except for reporting requirements in 4.2 items (2) through (10), registered in doc/catalogues/processor_conformance.json as S4.2-002 through S4.2-010.
Maximum image counts and program/data size or complexity beyond a computing system or processor capability are not specified here.
The mechanism for determining the number of images is outside this document; this exclusion creates no local image-count semantics or owner handoff.
Physical properties of images and their relationship to computational elements are outside this document.

Physical representation of quantities and processor rounding, approximation, or numeric computation methods are outside scope except where incorporated under Clause 17; this exclusion is not itself a floating-point requirement.
Physical properties of input/output records, files, and units are outside scope; this exclusion does not create logical I/O semantics or a local test oracle.
Physical properties and implementation of storage are outside scope.

review_rationale: Source registration for Clauses 1 and 2 and the compatibility subclauses 4.3-4.3.4 (batch246). Scope and normative-reference text is structural; compatibility statements that restate rules owned elsewhere cross-reference their owners (12.11.5, 19.4, C1598) instead of duplicating them. Source accounting only.
